Q: How to convert number of minutes to hh:mm format in TSQL? A:

Using TIMEFROMPARTS function:

SELECT t.duration,TIMEFROMPARTS(t.duration/60,t.duration%60,0,0,0) AS duration_time
FROM tab AS t;

Input:

CREATE TABLE tab(duration INT);
-- duration range 0-1439
INSERT INTO tab(duration)
VALUES(60),(80),(90),(150),(180),(1000);

Output:

+-----------+---------------+
| duration  | duration_time |
+-----------+---------------+
|       60  | 01:00:00      |
|       80  | 01:20:00      |
|       90  | 01:30:00      |
|      150  | 02:30:00      |
|      180  | 03:00:00      |
|     1000  | 16:40:00      |
+-----------+---------------+

Q: Login AJAX and codeigniter A:

Your problem is your controller. Your ajax code calls login() in your controller and passes two variable to it, but your login() method does not get them. The login() signature must be like this:

public function login($Variable_one, $Variable_two)

Q: running pip install from python 2.7.5 A:

You probably should (re)install a new version of pip explicitly for the new Python version. On pip installation instructions page it says that

pip works with CPython versions 2.6, 2.7, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and also pypy.

While installing, be sure to use the newer version of Python instead of the old one.

Q: PowerShell : how to zip directory based on file name A:

NOTE

The following answer assumes Compress-Archive can't be used due to the 2GB+ limitation. This was pointed out by OP in this comment.

There is a problem if using $input in:

$input = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($file.FullName)
$input.CopyTo($entry.Open())
$input.Dispose()

This is an automatic variable in PowerShell which's type is already defined:

$input.GetType() # System.Collections.ArrayList+ArrayListEnumeratorSimple

Your code might work using it but it's not recommended. If you were to inspect it, its content (a file stream in this case) would be gone... you should change it to something different.

$input = 'hello'
$input -eq 'hello' # True
$input             # As soon as you inspect it, there is nothing

The main issue is where you're presumably trying create a entry for the folder having the same name as the XML (TEST123 in the example), there is no such thing as [System.IO.Path]::OpenRead(...) and opening a stream for a directory isn't a thing in .NET; even if it did, Stream.CopyTo(Stream) wouldn't handle the recursive copy of the contents of that folders and you're also not handling the zip entry creation for each child item in that directory.

The easiest way to solve your issue with a .NET API is to use ZipFile.CreateFromDirectory, it doesn't have the 2GB limitation:

foreach ($file in $files) {
    try {
        # Create the destination zip path (same folder, same name, .zip extension)
        $zipPath = Join-Path $sourceDir ($file.BaseName + '.ZIP')

        [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::CreateFromDirectory(
            $file.DirectoryName, # DirectoryName is the absolute path of the parent directory
            $zipPath,
            [System.IO.Compression.CompressionLevel]::Optimal
            $false)              # Don't include base directory

        Write-Host "Zipped '$($file.Name)' to '$zipPath'"

    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Failed to zip '$($file.Name)': $_"
    }
}

Using the argument includeBaseDirectory set to $false your zip archive should become:

TEST123.ZIP
├── TEST123.XML
└── TEST123
    └── etc...

Another option is to use Compress-ZipArchive, I made this cmdlet specifically to overcome the 2GB limitation while having a similar usage as Compress-Archive.

If going this route, install the module first:

Install-Module PSCompression -Scope CurrentUser

Then the loop logic is very simple:

foreach ($file in $files) {
    try {
        # Create the destination zip path (same folder, same name, .zip extension)
        $zipPath = Join-Path $sourceDir ($file.BaseName + '.ZIP')

        # \* = Compress the contents of this folder but not the folder itself
        Compress-ZipArchive "$($file.DirectoryName)\*" -Destination $zipPath -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-Host "Zipped '$($file.Name)' to '$zipPath'"

    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Failed to zip '$($file.Name)': $_"
    }
}
